question:
An annual allowance for wear and tear of a capital goods is known as ______.

[SSC MTS 2022]
options: gross investment
devaluation
depreciation
disinvestment
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is depreciation

Explanation:
Depreciation refers to the annual allowance for the wear and tear or reduction in value of a capital good (such as machinery, buildings, equipment etc.) over time due to usage and obsolescence. It is a non-cash expense recorded in financial statements to allocate the cost of the asset over its useful life. Depreciation serves two main purposes: 1) Matching principle in accounting by spreading costs, and 2) Reducing taxable income. Common methods include straight-line and diminishing balance methods. It's crucial for capital budgeting and investment decisions as it affects cash flows and profitability calculations.

Extra Facts:
In national income accounting, net investment equals gross investment minus depreciation. Different industries have varying depreciation rates based on asset types. Governments sometimes use accelerated depreciation as fiscal policy to stimulate investment. Economic depreciation differs from accounting depreciation as it considers market value changes. The concept of accumulated depreciation appears in balance sheets as a contra-asset account. Capital consumption allowance is the macroeconomic term for total depreciation in an economy.

question_hi:
किसी पूँजीगत वस्तु की टूट-फूट के लिए वार्षिक भत्ता__________ कहलाता है

[SSC MTS 2022]
options_hi: सकल निवेश
अवमूल्यन
मूल्यह्रास
विनिवेश
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है मूल्यह्रास

Explanation:
मूल्यह्रास (Depreciation) किसी पूँजीगत वस्तु (जैसे मशीन, भवन, उपकरण आदि) के उपयोग और समय के साथ होने वाली टूट-फूट या मूल्य में कमी को दर्शाता है। यह एक वार्षिक भत्ता है जिसे कंपनियाँ अपने वित्तीय विवरणों में दर्ज करती हैं। मूल्यह्रास का उद्देश्य पूँजीगत वस्तु की लागत को उसके उपयोगी जीवनकाल में वितरित करना है। यह लेखांकन और कराधान में महत्वपूर्ण है क्योंकि यह कंपनी के कर योग्य लाभ को कम करता है। मूल्यह्रास की गणना विभिन्न विधियों (जैसे सीधी रेखा विधि, घटती शेष विधि) से की जा सकती है।

Extra Facts:
पूँजीगत वस्तुओं का मूल्यह्रास अर्थव्यवस्था में पूँजी निर्माण और निवेश निर्णयों को प्रभावित करता है। यह राष्ट्रीय आय लेखांकन में भी महत्वपूर्ण है, जहाँ शुद्ध निवेश (Net Investment) की गणना सकल निवेश (Gross Investment) में से मूल्यह्रास घटाकर की जाती है। मूल्यह्रास की दर पूँजीगत वस्तु की प्रकृति और उद्योग के अनुसार भिन्न हो सकती है। सरकारें कभी-कभी त्वरित मूल्यह्रास (Accelerated Depreciation) की अनुमति देकर निवेश को प्रोत्साहित करती हैं।

question:
Which of the following is NOT a direct tax in India?

[RRC GROUP D]
options: Income Tax
Corporate tax
Excise Tax
Capital Gain tax
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Excise Tax

Explanation:
A direct tax is imposed directly on an individual or entity and cannot be shifted to another party. Income Tax, Corporate Tax, and Capital Gains Tax are all direct taxes as they are levied directly on the income of individuals or companies. Excise Tax is an indirect tax because it is imposed on the production or sale of goods and services, and its burden can be passed on to the end consumer. In India, the excise tax has been replaced by the Goods and Services Tax (GST), which is an indirect tax.

Extra Facts:
Examples of direct taxes include property tax, gift tax, and wealth tax. These taxes are paid directly to the government. Indirect taxes like VAT, service tax, and customs duty are paid indirectly by consumers. A significant portion of India's tax structure comes from indirect taxes, which are a major source of revenue for the government.

question_hi:
निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा भारत में प्रत्यक्ष कर नहीं है?

[RRC GROUP D]
options_hi: आयकर
निगम कर
उत्पाद कर
पूंजीगत लाभ कर
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है उत्पाद कर

Explanation:
प्रत्यक्ष कर वह कर होता है जो सीधे व्यक्ति या संस्था पर लगाया जाता है और जिसे दूसरे व्यक्ति पर टाला नहीं जा सकता। आयकर, निगम कर, और पूंजीगत लाभ कर सभी प्रत्यक्ष कर हैं क्योंकि ये सीधे व्यक्ति या कंपनी की आय पर लगाए जाते हैं। उत्पाद कर एक अप्रत्यक्ष कर है क्योंकि यह वस्तुओं और सेवाओं के उत्पादन या बिक्री पर लगाया जाता है और इसका भार अंतिम उपभोक्ता पर डाला जा सकता है। भारत में, उत्पाद कर को जीएसटी (GST) द्वारा प्रतिस्थापित कर दिया गया है, जो एक अप्रत्यक्ष कर है।

Extra Facts:
प्रत्यक्ष कर का उदाहरण संपत्ति कर, उपहार कर, और धन कर भी हैं। ये कर सरकार को सीधे जमा किए जाते हैं। अप्रत्यक्ष कर जैसे वैट, सेवा कर, और सीमा शुल्क, उपभोक्ताओं द्वारा अप्रत्यक्ष रूप से भुगतान किए जाते हैं। भारत में कर संरचना का एक बड़ा हिस्सा अप्रत्यक्ष करों से आता है, जो सरकार के लिए राजस्व का प्रमुख स्रोत है।

question:
Which of the following is NOT a GST rate slab in India?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: 5%
18%
10%
28%
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 10%

Explanation:
In India, the GST (Goods and Services Tax) has four main rate slabs - 5%, 12%, 18%, and 28%. Additionally, some goods are taxed at 0% (zero rate) and 3% (special rate). The 10% rate is not a valid GST slab in India, making it the correct answer. GST rates are designed such that essential goods have lower rates, while luxury items attract higher rates.

Extra Facts:
GST was implemented in India on 1st July 2017 and is a value-added tax (VAT) system. GST includes CGST (Central GST), SGST (State GST), and IGST (Integrated GST). The highest rate of 28% applies to luxury items like cars, cigarettes, etc., while 5% is levied on essential goods like milk, eggs, etc.

☛ How many types of taxes are under GST? → CGST, SGST, IGST
☛ Which goods attract 5% GST? → Essential goods
☛ What type of tax is GST? → Value-added tax

Extra Facts:
GST भारत में 1 जुलाई 2017 से लागू हुआ था और यह एक मूल्य वर्धित कर (VAT) प्रणाली है। GST के तहत CGST (केंद्रीय GST), SGST (राज्य GST), और IGST (एकीकृत GST) शामिल हैं। 28% की दर सबसे अधिक है और यह विलासिता की वस्तुओं जैसे कार, सिगरेट आदि पर लागू होती है। 5% की दर आवश्यक वस्तुओं जैसे दूध, अंडे आदि पर लागू होती है।

question:
____ taxes are levied by the State Government in India.

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Customs
Corporation
Excise duty on liquor
Capital gains
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Excise duty on liquor

Explanation:
In India, 'Excise duty on liquor' is levied by the State Governments, which is a type of indirect tax. This tax is a significant revenue source for state governments. According to the Constitution, 'production and sale of alcohol' is a state subject, hence state governments are authorized to impose taxes on it. Other options like 'Customs' (levied by the Central Government), 'Corporation Tax' (levied by the Central Government), and 'Capital Gains' (can be levied by both Centre and State) are not primary taxes of state governments.

Extra Facts:
Excise Duty is an indirect tax imposed at the manufacturing level in India. It is divided into 'Central Excise Duty' and 'State Excise Duty'. Excise duty on alcohol, petroleum products, and narcotics is levied by state governments, while other goods are taxed by the Central Government. This tax is 'outside GST' and remains an independent revenue source for states.

question_hi:

पूंजीगत लाभ

Explanation:
भारत में राज्य सरकारें 'शराब पर उत्पाद शुल्क' लगाती हैं, जो एक प्रकार का अप्रत्यक्ष कर है। यह कर राज्य सरकार के लिए महत्वपूर्ण राजस्व स्रोत है। संविधान के अनुसार, 'शराब का उत्पादन और बिक्री' राज्य सूची का विषय है, इसलिए राज्य सरकारें इस पर कर लगाने के लिए अधिकृत हैं। अन्य विकल्प जैसे 'सीमाशुल्क' (केंद्र सरकार द्वारा लगाया जाता है), 'निगम कर' (केंद्र सरकार द्वारा लगाया जाता है), और 'पूंजीगत लाभ' (केंद्र और राज्य दोनों द्वारा लगाया जा सकता है) राज्य सरकार के प्राथमिक कर नहीं हैं।

Extra Facts:
उत्पाद शुल्क एक अप्रत्यक्ष कर है जो भारत में विनिर्माण स्तर पर लगाया जाता है। यह 'केंद्रीय उत्पाद शुल्क' और 'राज्य उत्पाद शुल्क' में विभाजित है। शराब, पेट्रोलियम उत्पाद, और नशीले पदार्थों पर उत्पाद शुल्क राज्य सरकारों द्वारा लगाया जाता है, जबकि अन्य वस्तुओं पर केंद्र सरकार द्वारा। यह कर 'जीएसटी' (GST) के अंतर्गत नहीं आता है और राज्यों के लिए एक स्वतंत्र राजस्व स्रोत बना हुआ है।

question:
In which year was Service Tax first imposed in India?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: 2002
1995
1998
1994
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 1994

Explanation:
Service Tax was first imposed in India in 1994 under the Finance Act, 1994, and it came into effect on 1st July 1994. The tax was introduced to increase government revenue by taxing services. Initially, it was levied on only 3 services (telephone, insurance, and stockbroking), but later it was expanded to cover many other services. Service Tax was abolished in 2017 after the implementation of GST (Goods and Services Tax).

Extra Facts:
Service Tax was an indirect tax levied on the supply of services. The initial rate was 5%, which was later increased to 15%. The tax was collected by the Central Government but shared between the Centre and States. Under GST, services are also taxed, but it is a unified tax system applicable to both goods and services.

question:
When was the Goods and Services Tax (GST) implemented in India?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: 1st April 2018
1st July 2017
1st July 2018
1st April 2017
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 1st July 2017

Explanation:
The Goods and Services Tax (GST) was implemented in India on 1st July 2017. It was a major tax reform that replaced multiple indirect taxes with a unified tax structure. GST is a value-added tax (VAT) system based on the principle of 'One Nation, One Tax'. It simplified tax administration and reduced tax evasion. GST is divided into three categories: CGST (Central GST), SGST (State GST), and IGST (Integrated GST).

Extra Facts:
The 101st Constitutional Amendment (2016) was passed to implement GST. This tax system improves supply chain efficiency and reduces the cascading effect of taxes. Under GST, goods and services are taxed at different slabs: 5%, 12%, 18%, and 28%.

question:
When was the Direct Tax Code Bill introduced in the Parliament of India?

[SSC CHSL 2022]
options: 2010
2005
2020
2015
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 2010

Explanation:
The Direct Tax Code (DTC) Bill was introduced in the Indian Parliament in August 2010. This bill aimed to simplify and make the direct tax system in India more transparent. Its primary objective was to consolidate the Income Tax Act, 1961, and other direct tax laws. The bill was designed to ease the tax process for taxpayers and reduce tax evasion. However, the bill has not been passed yet, and discussions are still ongoing.

Extra Facts:
Direct taxes are levied directly on individuals and companies, such as income tax and corporate tax. In India, direct taxes are collected by the Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT). The Direct Tax Code aims to make the tax system more efficient and equitable. It seeks to simplify tax rates for taxpayers and streamline tax exemptions. The DTC is part of India's broader tax reforms to enhance compliance and reduce litigation.

question:
In which type of tax is the marginal tax rate higher than the average tax rate?

[SSC CPO 2023]
options: Proportional
Regressive
Digressive
Progressive
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Progressive

Explanation:
A progressive tax is a tax where the tax rate increases as the taxable income increases. In this system, the marginal tax rate is always higher than the average tax rate. This happens because higher income brackets are taxed at higher rates, meaning each additional rupee earned is taxed more than the average rate paid on previous income. Progressive taxation helps reduce income inequality and generates higher revenue for the government.

Extra Facts:
The progressive tax system is commonly used in developed economies to promote economic justice. In contrast, a regressive tax imposes a heavier burden on low-income earners, while a proportional tax applies the same rate to all income levels. A digressive tax is a hybrid of progressive and proportional systems, where the tax rate increases up to a certain limit and then becomes flat. India's income tax is an example of a progressive tax structure.

Expected Questions for Upcoming Exams :

☛ Example of a regressive tax? → Sales Tax
☛ What type of tax is income tax in India? → Progressive Tax
☛ How does the tax rate change in a digressive tax? → Increases up to a limit, then becomes flat
☛ Main objective of progressive tax? → Reduce income inequality
question_hi:
किस प्रकार के कर में सीमांत कर दर, औसत कर दर से अधिक होती है?

[SSC CPO 2023]
options_hi: समानुपातिक (Proportional)
प्रतिगामी (Regressive)
व्यतिक्रमी (Digressive)
प्रगामी (Progressive)
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है प्रगामी (Progressive)

Explanation:
प्रगामी कर वह कर है जिसमें कर की दर आय में वृद्धि के साथ बढ़ती है। इस प्रणाली में, सीमांत कर दर (Marginal Tax Rate) हमेशा औसत कर दर (Average Tax Rate) से अधिक होती है। ऐसा इसलिए होता है क्योंकि उच्च आय वर्ग पर कर की दर अधिक लगाई जाती है, जिससे प्रत्येक अतिरिक्त रुपये पर लगने वाला कर (सीमांत दर) पहले से भुगतान किए गए करों के औसत से अधिक हो जाता है। यह आय की असमानता को कम करने में मदद करता है और सरकार को अधिक राजस्व प्रदान करता है।

Extra Facts:
प्रगामी कर प्रणाली का उपयोग अक्सर विकसित देशों में किया जाता है क्योंकि यह आर्थिक न्याय को बढ़ावा देती है। इसके विपरीत, प्रतिगामी कर (Regressive Tax) में निम्न आय वर्ग पर कर का बोझ अधिक होता है, जबकि समानुपातिक कर (Proportional Tax) में सभी आय स्तरों पर कर की दर समान होती है। व्यतिक्रमी कर (Digressive Tax) प्रगामी और समानुपातिक कर का मिश्रण है, जहां कर दर एक निश्चित सीमा तक बढ़ती है और फिर स्थिर हो जाती है।

question:
_____ restrict/s imports and help/s domestic producers from foreign competition.
(A) Tariffs
(B) Quotas

[SSC GD 2022]
options: Only B
Only A
Neither A nor B
Both A and B
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Both A and B

Explanation:
Both Tariffs and Quotas are trade policy instruments used to restrict imports and protect domestic producers from foreign competition. Tariffs are taxes imposed on imported goods, making them more expensive and less competitive. Quotas set a physical limit on the quantity of imports, reducing foreign goods' availability in the domestic market. Both measures provide protection to local industries and control import levels.

Extra Facts:
Tariffs can also generate government revenue, while Quotas directly limit import quantities. These tools are often used in protectionist policies in international trade. While they help boost domestic employment and industries, they may also increase prices for consumers and restrict global trade.

question:
__________is an Islamic finance term referring to the obligation that an individual has to donate a certain proportion of wealth each year to charitable causes.

[RRC GROUP D]
options: Mudarabah
Ijarah
Zakat
Musharakah
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Zakat

Explanation:
In Islamic finance, Zakat is a mandatory charitable contribution, requiring eligible Muslims to donate a fixed portion (typically 2.5%) of their wealth and income to the poor and needy. It is one of the Five Pillars of Islam and aims to reduce economic inequality, promote social justice, and support vulnerable groups in society. Zakat can only be paid to specific categories (e.g., the poor, debtors, travelers) as mentioned in the Quran.

Extra Facts:
• Zakat is calculated on wealth exceeding Nisab (a minimum threshold).
• It applies to assets like cash, gold, trade goods, and agricultural produce—not personal-use items.
• Zakat differs from Sadaqah (voluntary charity)—Zakat is obligatory, while Sadaqah is optional.
• In Islamic banking, Zakat is viewed as a social tax ensuring economic stability.

☛ What is Mudarabah? → Profit-sharing between capital provider and manager
☛ What is Riba in Islamic economics? → Interest, which is prohibited
☛ What are Sukuk? → Islamic bonds or Sharia-compliant financial certificates
question_hi:
इस्लाम में __________, किसी व्यक्ति द्वारा प्रति वर्ष कमाए जाने वाले कुल धन के उस हिस्से को कहा जाता है, जिसे वह धर्मार्थ व्यय करता है।

[RRC GROUP D]
options_hi: मुदरबाह(Mudarabah)
इज़राह(Ijarah)
जकात(Zakat)
मुशरकाह(Musharakah)
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है जकात (Zakat)

Explanation:
इस्लामी अर्थशास्त्र में, 'जकात' एक अनिवार्य धर्मार्थ दान है जिसे हर सक्षम मुस्लिम व्यक्ति को अपनी संपत्ति और आय के एक निश्चित हिस्से (आमतौर पर 2.5%) के रूप में गरीबों और जरूरतमंदों को देना होता है। यह इस्लाम के 'पाँच स्तंभों' में से एक है और इसका उद्देश्य आर्थिक असमानता को कम करना, सामाजिक न्याय को बढ़ावा देना और समुदाय के कमजोर वर्गों की सहायता करना है। जकात का भुगतान केवल विशिष्ट श्रेणियों (जैसे गरीब, कर्जदार, यात्री आदि) पर किया जा सकता है, जिसका उल्लेख कुरान में किया गया है।

Extra Facts:
• जकात की गणना 'निसाब' (एक न्यूनतम धन राशि) से अधिक की संपत्ति पर लागू होती है।
• यह केवल नकद, सोना-चांदी, व्यापारिक सामान और कृषि उपज जैसी संपत्तियों पर लागू होता है, न कि व्यक्तिगत उपयोग की वस्तुओं पर।
• जकात और 'सदक़ा' (ऐच्छिक दान) में अंतर है—जकात अनिवार्य है, जबकि सदक़ा स्वैच्छिक।
• इस्लामी बैंकिंग में, जकात को एक 'सामाजिक कर' के रूप में देखा जाता है जो आर्थिक स्थिरता सुनिश्चित करता है।

question:
What is a Per unit Tax ( or Unit Tax )?

[NTPC CBT 2]
options: A tax that the government imposes per unit purchase on imports
A tax that the government imposes per unit sale of output.
A tax that the factory imposes per unit sale of output.
A tax that the factory imposes on total unit purchase on imports.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is A tax that the government imposes per unit sale of output.

Explanation:
A per unit tax is a tax imposed by the government on each unit of output sold. It is a fixed amount levied per unit, such as ₹5 per kilogram. This tax shifts the supply curve upwards, leading to an increase in the equilibrium price and a decrease in the equilibrium quantity in the market. It is a significant source of government revenue and is often used to control negative externalities (e.g., pollution). The burden of this tax is shared between producers and consumers based on the elasticity of demand and supply.

Extra Facts:
A per unit tax differs from an ad-valorem tax, which is a percentage of the product's price. Per unit taxes are commonly applied to goods like tobacco, petrol, and alcohol. The tax incidence (who bears the burden of the tax) depends on the elasticity of demand and supply. If demand is inelastic, consumers bear most of the tax burden, whereas if supply is inelastic, producers bear it. Governments use such taxes to discourage harmful consumption while generating revenue.

☛ What is a negative externality? → Unwanted impact on society
☛ What is a source of government revenue? → Tax and non-tax revenue

Explanation:

question:
Which of the following is NOT a tax subsumed under GST in India?

[NTPC CBT 2]
options: Service tax
Central excise duty
Additional custom duty
Income tax
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Income tax

Explanation:
GST (Goods and Services Tax) is an indirect tax in India that has subsumed several older taxes. It includes taxes like service tax, central excise duty, and additional custom duty. However, income tax is a direct tax and does not fall under the purview of GST. The aim of GST is to unify indirect taxes, whereas income tax is levied on the income of individuals and companies and is paid directly to the government.

Extra Facts:
GST was implemented on 1st July 2017 and is of three types: CGST (Central GST), SGST (State GST), and IGST (Integrated GST). GST has simplified tax administration and reduced tax evasion. It is based on a value-added tax (VAT) system that imposes tax only at the final stage of consumption.

question:
What makes imported goods more expensive?

[SSC GD 2022]
options: Custom Made goods
Rarity in nature
Superior Quality
Tariffs
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Tariffs

Explanation:
Imported goods become more expensive primarily due to 'Tariffs'. Tariffs are taxes imposed by the government on imported goods, aimed at protecting domestic industries and increasing government revenue. This tax increases the price of imported goods, making them more expensive in the domestic market. Additionally, transportation costs, exchange rates, and import quotas also affect the price of imported goods.

Extra Facts:
Tariffs are of two types: Specific Tariff and Ad-valorem Tariff. Specific tariffs are levied based on the quantity of goods, while ad-valorem tariffs are based on a percentage of the goods' value. Tariffs not only increase prices but also impact international trade. It is part of the 'Protectionism' policy, which shields domestic producers from foreign competition.

☛ What is a specific tariff? → Tax based on the quantity of goods
☛ What is an ad-valorem tariff? → Tax based on a percentage of the goods' value
☛ What is the purpose of protectionism? → To safeguard domestic industries
☛ What is an import quota? → A limit on the quantity of goods that can be imported

solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है प्रशुल्कों

Explanation:
आयातित सामान अधिक महंगा होता है मुख्य रूप से 'प्रशुल्कों (Tariffs)' के कारण। प्रशुल्क सरकार द्वारा आयातित वस्तुओं पर लगाया जाने वाला कर है, जिसका उद्देश्य घरेलू उद्योगों को संरक्षण प्रदान करना और सरकारी राजस्व में वृद्धि करना होता है। यह कर आयातित वस्तुओं की कीमत को बढ़ा देता है, जिससे वे घरेलू बाजार में अधिक महंगी हो जाती हैं। इसके अलावा, परिवहन लागत, मुद्रा विनिमय दर और आयात कोटा भी आयातित सामान की कीमत को प्रभावित करते हैं।

Extra Facts:
प्रशुल्क दो प्रकार के होते हैं: विशिष्ट प्रशुल्क (Specific Tariff) और मूल्य-आधारित प्रशुल्क (Ad-valorem Tariff)। विशिष्ट प्रशुल्क वस्तु की मात्रा पर लगाया जाता है, जबकि मूल्य-आधारित प्रशुल्क वस्तु के मूल्य के प्रतिशत के रूप में लगाया जाता है। प्रशुल्क न केवल कीमतें बढ़ाते हैं बल्कि अंतर्राष्ट्रीय व्यापार को भी प्रभावित करते हैं। यह 'संरक्षणवाद (Protectionism)' की नीति का हिस्सा है, जो घरेलू उत्पादकों को विदेशी प्रतिस्पर्धा से बचाता है।

question:
If the tax rate increases with the taxable base, then this type of taxation is called:

[SSC MTS 2024]
options: digressive
progressive
regressive
proportional
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is progressive

Explanation:
Progressive taxation is a system where the tax rate increases as the taxable base (income/wealth) increases. This means higher-income individuals pay a larger percentage of their income as tax compared to lower-income individuals. It aims to reduce income inequality and promote social justice by redistributing wealth. For example, in India, income tax slabs are structured such that higher earners face higher tax rates. This aligns with the 'ability-to-pay' principle in economics.

Extra Facts:
Progressive taxes are crucial for wealth redistribution and funding public welfare programs. In contrast, a regressive tax (e.g., sales tax) burdens lower-income groups more as the rate decreases with income. A proportional tax (flat tax) applies the same rate to all income levels. Progressive taxation is a key tool in fiscal policy to address economic disparities.

Extra Facts:
प्रगामी कराधान का उद्देश्य धन के पुनर्वितरण (Redistribution of Wealth) को सुनिश्चित करना है। यह अमीरों से अधिक कर लेकर गरीबों को सुविधाएं प्रदान करता है। इसके विपरीत, प्रतिगामी कर (Regressive Tax) में कर की दर आय के साथ घटती है, जैसे वैट या सेल्स टैक्स। आनुपातिक कर (Proportional Tax) में कर की दर सभी आय स्तरों पर समान होती है।

question:
_______________ is one of the taxes, where the impact lies on the person for whom it is legally imposed.

[SSC CHSL 2021]
options: Direct tax
Indirect tax
Goods and services tax
Value added tax
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Direct tax

Explanation:
A direct tax is a tax where the impact and burden fall on the same person upon whom it is legally imposed. The burden of this tax cannot be shifted to another person. Examples include income tax, property tax, and corporate tax. These taxes are paid directly to the government, and their impact is clearly on the taxpayer. Direct taxes are usually progressive, meaning higher-income individuals pay taxes at a higher rate.

Extra Facts:
The key difference between direct and indirect taxes is that the burden of indirect taxes (e.g., GST, VAT) ultimately falls on the consumer, even if collected by the seller. Direct taxes are a significant source of revenue for the government and help in income and wealth redistribution. In India, the Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) is responsible for administering direct taxes.

question:

GST cannot be collected by the state government.
July 1st is celebrated as GST day by the Central board of Excise and Customs.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is GST cannot be collected by the state government.

Explanation:
GST (Goods and Services Tax) is an indirect tax collected by both state and central governments. It was implemented in India on 1st July 2017. France was indeed the first country to introduce GST in 1954. GST Day is celebrated on 1st July, as declared by the Central Board of Excise and Customs.

Extra Facts:
GST is divided into three types: CGST (Central GST), SGST (State GST), and IGST (Integrated GST). CGST and SGST apply to intra-state transactions, while IGST is levied on inter-state transactions. GST simplified the tax structure and reduced tax evasion. Under GST, tax rates are 5%, 12%, 18%, and 28%, with exemptions for certain goods and services.

question:
______ is a tax system that collects a greater share of income from those with high incomes than from those with lower incomes.

[SSC CGL 2021]
options: Proportional tax
Regressive tax
Payroll tax
Progressive tax
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Progressive tax

Explanation:
Progressive Tax is a tax system where the tax rate increases as the taxable income increases. This means that high-income earners pay a larger percentage of their income in taxes compared to low-income earners. It helps in reducing income inequality and promotes social justice. For example, in India, income tax rates are progressive, where higher income slabs attract higher tax rates. This system is based on the 'Ability to Pay Principle,' which states that those who earn more should contribute more to the government's revenue.

Extra Facts:
Major Types of Tax Systems:
1. Proportional Tax: A flat tax rate applied to all income levels, e.g., GST.
2. Regressive Tax: Lower-income individuals pay a higher percentage of their income in taxes compared to high-income earners, e.g., sales tax.
3. Payroll Tax: Levied on employees and employers to fund social security schemes.
Significance of Progressive Tax: It reduces economic inequality, funds public services, and promotes social welfare by redistributing wealth.

Explanation:
In India, under the Goods and Services Tax (GST), there are four primary tax rates: 5%, 12%, 18%, and 28%. These rates are based on the nature and necessity of goods and services. The 5% rate applies to essential items (e.g., milk, eggs, vegetables), while 12% and 18% are levied on mid-range products (e.g., processed food, electronics). The 28% rate is imposed on luxury and demerit goods (e.g., cigarettes, fast food). GST aims to implement a 'One Nation, One Tax' system, simplifying and making taxation transparent.

Extra Facts:
GST was implemented on 1st July 2017. It also includes a zero rate (0%) for highly essential items (e.g., grains, fresh meat). Additionally, certain items (e.g., petrol, alcohol) are excluded from GST. GST has three components: CGST (Central GST), SGST (State GST), and IGST (Integrated GST for interstate transactions).

हल: सही उत्तर है 1 जुलाई 2017

Explanation:
वस्तु और सेवा कर (GST) भारत में 1 जुलाई 2017 से लागू हुआ। यह एक अप्रत्यक्ष कर है जिसने कई पुराने करों जैसे केंद्रीय उत्पाद शुल्क (Excise Duty), सेवा कर (Service Tax), वैट (VAT) आदि को समाप्त कर दिया। GST का उद्देश्य 'एक राष्ट्र, एक कर' की अवधारणा को लागू करना था, जिससे कर प्रणाली सरल और पारदर्शी हो सके। यह कर तीन स्तरों पर लगाया जाता है: केंद्रीय GST (CGST), राज्य GST (SGST), और एकीकृत GST (IGST)। GST लागू होने से पहले इसे संसद में 101वें संविधान संशोधन अधिनियम, 2016 के तहत पारित किया गया था।

Extra Facts:
GST को वस्तु और सेवा कर परिषद (GST Council) द्वारा प्रबंधित किया जाता है, जिसकी अध्यक्षता केंद्रीय वित्त मंत्री करते हैं। GST के तहत कर की चार दरें हैं: 5%, 12%, 18%, और 28%। कुछ आवश्यक वस्तुओं जैसे दूध, अनाज आदि पर शून्य दर (0%) लागू है। GST लागू होने से कर चोरी (Tax Evasion) में कमी आई है और कर संग्रह (Tax Revenue) में वृद्धि हुई है। यह भारत की अर्थव्यवस्था को एकीकृत बाजार (Unified Market) बनाने की दिशा में एक महत्वपूर्ण कदम है।
